introduction_markdown:
This paper is arranged in three sections, A, B and C. Section A: answer ALL 5 questions; you will be graded for the best 4 answers. Section B: answer ALL TWO questions in this section. Section C: answer 2 questions out of 3; if you attempt more than 2 questions, only the first 2 will be considered. In calculations, you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators are allowed. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

**Useful data:** relative atomic masses H = 1.0, C = 12.0, O = 16.0, Na = 23.0, Cu = 64.0, Cl = 35.5, K = 39.0, N = 14.0, S = 32.0; 1 faraday = 96000 coulombs; molar volume of a gas at r.t.p. = 24000 cm$^3$; specific heat capacity of water = 4.2 J g$^{-1}$ $^\circ$C$^{-1}$; Avogadro number = $6.02\times10^{23}$; $0^\circ$C = 273 K.

Labels fell off from 3 identical bottles containing the following chemicals: Calcium chloride, Sodium Sulphate and Iron (II) bromide.

In order to identify the content of each bottle, a student was provided with the following reagents: aqueous Barium Chloride, aqueous Sodium hydroxide, aqueous Silver nitrate, Dilute HCl and material for flame test.

Complete the following tables that show the procedure used by the student and the observations.

questions.corrige_markdown:
| BOTTLE | Procedure | Observation |
|---|---|---|
| Containing Calcium chloride | (i) Flame test: dip a clean platinum (or nichrome) wire in the solution and hold it in a non-luminous Bunsen flame. | (i) **Brick-red flame** (calcium ions). |
| | (ii) Add aqueous sodium hydroxide drop by drop, then in excess. | (ii) **White precipitate** of calcium hydroxide, **insoluble in excess** sodium hydroxide. |

Equation for (ii): $\mathrm{Ca^{2+}(aq)} + 2\mathrm{OH^-(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{Ca(OH)_2(s)}$. (Alternative test for the chloride ion: add aqueous silver nitrate, which gives a white precipitate of silver chloride, $\mathrm{Ag^+} + \mathrm{Cl^-} \rightarrow \mathrm{AgCl}$.)

questions.corrige_markdown:
| BOTTLE | Procedure | Observation |
|---|---|---|
| Containing Sodium Sulphate | (i) Flame test with a clean wire. | (i) **Golden-yellow flame** (sodium ions). |
| | (ii) Add aqueous barium chloride, then add dilute hydrochloric acid. | (ii) **White precipitate** of barium sulphate, which is **insoluble in dilute HCl** (sulphate ion confirmed). |

Equation for (ii): $\mathrm{Ba^{2+}(aq)} + \mathrm{SO_4^{2-}(aq)} \rightarrow \mathrm{BaSO_4(s)}$. The acid is added to dissolve any carbonate or sulphite precipitate, which would otherwise give a false result.

questions.enonce_markdown:
The following setup was used to prepare and test for a gas in the laboratory

![fig-1](gce-ol-chemistry-2022-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_7_fig_1.png)

(i) What do you observe in the tube containing $\mathrm{K_2Cr_2O_7}$ solution?

(ii) Identify the gas produced in the first test tube A

(iii) State one physical test for the gas produced in test tube A *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) The **orange solution turns green**: the dichromate(VI) ions are reduced to chromium(III) ions by the gas.

(ii) **Sulphur dioxide, $\mathrm{SO_2}$**, produced by $\mathrm{Na_2SO_3} + 2\mathrm{HCl} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{NaCl} + \mathrm{H_2O} + \mathrm{SO_2}$.

(iii) Sulphur dioxide is a colourless gas with a **sharp, choking (pungent) smell** (smelt cautiously by wafting). It is also denser than air.

(Chemical confirmation: $\mathrm{Cr_2O_7^{2-}} + 3\mathrm{SO_2} + 2\mathrm{H^+} \rightarrow 2\mathrm{Cr^{3+}} + 3\mathrm{SO_4^{2-}} + \mathrm{H_2O}$.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
A student is given the following mixtures

(i) Ethanol/water (ii) Powdered Suphur/ Iron fillings (iii) Solid $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ / NaCl

Complete the following table by suggesting the method of separation.

| Mixture | Method of separation |
|---|---|
| Ethanol/water |  |
| Powdered Suphur/ Iron fillings |  |
| Solid $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ / NaCl |  |

*[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
| Mixture | Method of separation |
|---|---|
| Ethanol/water | **Fractional distillation** (ethanol boils at about 78 $^\circ$C, water at 100 $^\circ$C). |
| Powdered sulphur/iron filings | Use a **magnet**: iron filings are attracted and sulphur is left. |
| Solid $\mathrm{NH_4Cl}$ / NaCl | **Sublimation**: on heating, ammonium chloride sublimes and condenses on a cool surface; sodium chloride stays behind. |
